newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tanker chartering good, rates steady.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tanker chartering good, rates steady.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering in the focal Middle East market was strong, with rates holding steady, brokers said on Friday.
Tankers making trips to Japan settled at last done levels of W57.5, with rates for Eastern voyages placed at W55. VLCCs heading west could command W55, up W5 points from the previous day.
"It seems likely that rates will lift further next week, so you'll see a lot of selling going on," a London broker said.

"Current forecasts indicate between now and this time next month, there will be 50 VLCCs available, of which 15 are less than 10 years old, plus 15 ULCCs making a total of 65 vessels of 18.5 million tonnes," shipbrokers Gibsons said in their weekly report.
By mid-afternoon, five VLCCS had found employment, four travelling east and one west.

Crude tanker fixing in the Med remained good, with rates on Aframaxes up slightly. Brokers said Veba's chartering of the Mare Oriens, travelling Zuetina-Trieste at W102.5, was seen as typical of this market.
Suezmaxes were seen to have risen to W82.5, with room to improve.
Chartering in the UKC sector slowed, after yesterday's spate of fixtures. By the close of day, three Aframaxes had found employment, all travelling cross UKC. No transatlantic trips were seen.
Brokers said rates for 80,000 tonners remained at W107.5 as evidenced by Shell's chartering of a Neste vessel, travelling Fredericia- Sweden at W107.5.
